messages:
maria: Heads up — we just started seeing intermittent fnhook responses where the same field flips types (string vs number). Routing logic treats that as a hard schema reject and it spikes the reject_count.
aj: Can you paste a log example? @hao FYI.
hao: example log snippet: `{"user_id": 12345, "action": "charge", "attempts": 3}` vs `{"user_id": "12345", "action": "charge", "attempts": "3"}`. Link: https://logs.redwood/foo/alert/794321
lex: Oof. Do we currently count that as a full reject (billing/quota) or soft-validate? SLA math depends.
maria: Today it hits strict-validate -> reject path. That increments quota counters and triggers SLA alerting. It's noisy because many integrations send numeric ids as strings.
aj: Proposal: introduce a distinct signal `ambiguous_type` and treat it as a soft-fail by default (route to degrade path) while sampling payloads for telemetry. This avoids immediate billing shock.
hao: Implementation idea: add ValidationStatus.AMBIGUOUS_TYPE enum. Routing policy: AMBIGUOUS_TYPE -> SOFT_FAIL route with `fallback=true` metadata. Keep original payload available for reprocessing.
maria: Telemetry must expose `validation_reason=ambiguous_type`, `sample_rate`, and a redacted example payload. Sample rate default 0.01 to keep volume manageable. No raw PII in sampled blobs.
lex: Console UX: add a per-route filter showing ambiguous_type rate, trend, and example redacted payloads. Show cost impact if we route to degrade model vs strict reject. Make description clear for SREs and product.
aj: Canary: enable soft-fail for 5% of traffic first. Config flag `fnhook_ambig_softrollout` toggles behavior per-route/account.
hao: Quick config sketch:
```yaml
validation:
  ambiguous_type:
    handling: soft_fail
    sample_rate: 0.01
    canary_pct: 5
```
maria: Billing question: product asked whether we charge the original route cost or the fallback cost when ambiguous_type triggers a degrade. I think we should bill final execution only, but keep a separate metric for reject-like incidents.
lex: Agreed on final-execution billing. But keep a counter visible for `validation_impact` so finance can reconcile.
aj: SRE note: if fallback volumes spike, we need fallback-specific saturation alarms. Tie alerts to `route_id` + `fallback=true` dimension. ops-bot should fire on sustained >10% fallback rate.
ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT CONFIG UPDATED: fallback-rate threshold set to 10% for routegroup:fnhooks. Notification channel: #eng-oncall.
hao: I'll spike a prototype PR for the validator, routing change, and sampling export. Will include unit tests for coercion heuristics and a simple end-to-end canary plan.
maria: Please add a migration step for dashboards: we need to backfill `ambiguous_type` as a new timeseries so old graphs don't break. Also include runbook text describing when to flip to strict reject.
lex: We should also add an opt-in per-customer toggle in the Console for accounts that want strict mode immediately.
aj: Scheduling: 30m sync tomorrow to review PR and canary steps. I'll invite product and billing for the charge semantics convo.
maria: Thanks. Follow-ups: @hao open PR, @aj run canary, @lex finalize billing toggle.
